articles.title: Cluster Autoscaler not scaling down nodes: finding the reason in its logs
articles.excerpt: To cut node costs, you lowered the requests on your Pods and deployed. Requests are the amount of CPU and memory reserved for each container in a Pod. Allocatable is the amount of a node's CPU and mem…
articles.body: To cut node costs, you lowered the requests on your Pods and deployed. Requests are the amount of CPU and memory reserved for each container in a Pod. Allocatable is the amount of a node's CPU and memory that can be assigned to Pods. When you check it yourself, for the resource you lowered, the sum of requests on every node is below half of allocatable. Cluster Autoscaler (CA) removes a node when the sum of requests on it falls below half of allocatable. 1 Yet an hour later the node count hasn't changed, and the CA logs have no error lines (lines starting with E ). The bill doesn't go down until nodes are removed. CA logs, for each node, the reason it decided not to remove it. The line it prints tells you the reason and where to fix it.
articles.author: Kazu

articles.title: When I say a ticket is fully tested, how sure am I?

articles.body: Even after 6 years in the field, I ask myself this question all the time. Once I tested something that worked like a shared document with a version history. A specific action would create a new version of it. The original must never change. I created different documents and tried to change them in different ways, and it was all working pretty well. I was checking on all the obvious places, but the bugs are usually not there. I know that it isn’t realistic to verify that there are no bugs in the software. There are always the obvious ones, but it takes real critical thinking and understanding of the software to find the ones lurking in the shadows. I like to hold myself to high standards, and over the years I’ve learned where to look for them.

articles.body: Quando um gestor de fundos imobiliários me pergunta onde tokenizar seus ativos, percebo que a dúvida raramente é técnica — é estratégica. A escolha entre Ethereum e Stellar define custos, velocidade, compliance e, principalmente, a viabilidade de um projeto no mercado brasileiro. Depois de duas décadas implementando infraestrutura de TI e os últimos anos imerso em Web3, construí uma visão prática sobre quando cada rede faz sentido. Vou compartilhar isso de forma direta. O peso do custo e da velocidade na operação brasileira O Brasil é um mercado sensível a taxas. Tokenizar um recebível de R$ 50 mil não pode custar R$ 80 em gas fees — e é exatamente aqui que Ethereum frequentemente tropeça.

articles.title: Give the agent the existing form-library pattern, don’t invent a new useState form
articles.excerpt: The agent adds an “edit display name” form with four useState hooks, a hand-rolled errors object, and a disabled={loading} flag that does not match the existing submit button. The repo already uses Re…
articles.body: The agent adds an “edit display name” form with four useState hooks, a hand-rolled errors object, and a disabled={loading} flag that does not match the existing submit button. The repo already uses React Hook Form (or Formik, or the design-system useForm ) with a shared validation helper and a standard error message component. The new form ignores all of it, so the field chrome, the error announcement, and the submit policy look different from every other settings row. I’ve started treating a from-scratch useState form in a repo that already has a form library as a rewrite , not as a small UI addition. The library is there so validation, touched state, and submit errors stay consistent. Why the hand-rolled form shows up Tutorials start with useState .

articles.title: How to reduce AI costs: 9 ways that work in 2026
articles.excerpt: TL;DR. The fastest way to reduce AI costs is to stop paying top-model prices for every step. Turn the effort level down first. In Anthropic's own test, one model solved 87.4% of coding tasks at low ef…
articles.body: TL;DR. The fastest way to reduce AI costs is to stop paying top-model prices for every step. Turn the effort level down first. In Anthropic's own test , one model solved 87.4% of coding tasks at low effort for USD 0.11 each against 95.3% at high for USD 0.29. Running low then retrying only the failures at high reached about 97% for about USD 0.17. Then cache repeated prompts, batch work that can wait ( 50% off ), give simple steps to free or cheap models, and keep the strong model as the one that decides. I'm Denys, a Forward Deployed Engineer. I build AI agents and automations for small firms. This list is the one I use. It's for the owner who sees an AI line on the invoice growing and wants to know which levers move it.

articles.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
articles.excerpt: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity, and that verifies Einstein's greatest theory.
articles.body: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all?

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away.
